title: Rapper Pitbull Sets World Record For Largest Gathering Of People In Bald Caps
summary: Rapper Pitbull set the world record on July 10 for the largest gathering of people wearing bald caps with 22,141 of his fans.
story: Mr. Worldwide is out here, breaking world records.

Rapper Pitbull, who was born Armando Christian Pérez, set the world record on July 10 for the largest gathering of people wearing bald caps. A whopping 22,141 of the rapper’s fans, affectionately referred to as the “Bald-Es,” showed up to London’s BST Hyde Park festival to pull off the feat. The record was officially confirmed by the Guinness World Records.
Dale, indeed.
In a video capturing the official count, shared on the rapper’s social media, Pitbull can be seen ecstatically yelling, “Bald-E’s, we did it Bald-E’s! We did it Bald-E’s!”

For the gathering, thousands of fans showed up to the festival wearing not only bald caps, but also the rapper’s signature shades. Some took their outfits to another level, donning Pitbull’s legendary tie look, while others also drew on goatees for additional accuracy.
In order for the record to be official, Pitbull himself had to wear a bald cap, Will Munford, an official adjudicator for the Guinness World Records said, according to The Guardian.

The moment called for serious counting. So, 400 volunteers were onsite to individually check people, Munford said, according to the outlet. There was also “drone footage with 42 counters backstage,” Munford added.
The gathering was actually the brainchild of British podcaster Jack Remington, who floated the idea on TikTok in October 2025.

“The capacity of High Park is 65,000 people. That is easily enough to break the world record for the number of people cosplaying as Pitbull in one place at one time,” Remington said in the video. “There is only one man who can save us right now ... and I actually have one thing to say. Dale.”
Pitbull eventually got wind of the proposed record attempt and it was on from there.
Well, we can safely say that everyone had a good hair day that day.

title: Beyoncé, Blue Ivy Surprise Fans During Jay-Z’s Opening Night of ‘Reasonable Doubt’ Shows
summary: Jay-Z kicked off his shows at Yankee Stadium in celebration of the 30th anniversary of his album “Reasonable Doubt” along with the 25th anniversary of “The Blueprint” with performances by Beyoncé and Blue Ivy Carter.
story: He’s not just a businessman, or even a business, man — he’s also a family man.

Jay-Z kicked off the first of three headlining shows at New York’s Yankee Stadium on July 10 in celebration of the 30th anniversary of his album “Reasonable Doubt” along with the 25th anniversary of “The Blueprint.” To mark the special occasion, he brought out both wife Beyoncé and eldest daughter Blue Ivy Carter to perform by his side.

Beyoncé took the stage during Hov’s first song of the set, “Can’t Knock The Hustle.” Dressed in a custom Giuseppe di Morabito blazer and capri pants set that was embellished with oversized crystal pinstripes, the star brought the house down as she took over Mary J. Blige’s iconic hook.
“Give it up for my baby,” Beyoncé said, addressing the crowd. “He’s the man.”
Later on in the show, Blue Ivy Carter joined her father to perform his 1997 single “Feelin’ It.” The 14-year-old, wearing a Yankees-themed outfit, played the piano as Jay-Z rapped over the notes.
“Make some noise for the legendary Blue Ivy Carter,” the rapper said during the performance.
Hov’s opening night was filled with big-name guests and other surprise performances. In addition to his famous family members, he also brought out former rival Nas and Alicia Keys.

The shows come after years of few public performances from the legendary Brooklyn rapper. Yankee Stadium immortalized the occasion by gifting him three custom bats, representing the three nights of performances, according to the venue’s social media. The bats were designed by local artists Rafael Caraballo and Jeff Rose King.
Now, we can only imagine what his remaining two shows will bring.

title: Zendaya Shares The Sweet Way Tom Holland Broke The News She Was Cast In ‘The Odyssey’
summary: Zendaya, who plays Athena in the upcoming Christopher Nolan-directed film “The Odyssey,” said in an interview with the Associated Press that her husband Tom Holland was the one to deliver the news of her casting.
story: For Zendaya, some good news got even better with the help of her hubby Tom Holland.

The actress, who plays Athena in the upcoming Christopher Nolan-directed film “The Odyssey,” said in an interview with the Associated Press that Holland was the one to deliver the news of her casting. And it was simply epic.

As Z tells it, Holland – who plays Telemachus, the son of main character Odysseus — had already been cast in the film and was just returning from a meeting with Nolan. Zendaya told the AP that Holland, 30, handed her the film’s script, which the two had been reviewing together just the night before.
“He was like, ‘Read it again.’ And I was like, ‘OK,’” Zendaya, 29, recalled to the AP. “And he was like, ‘But now, think of Athena.’”
It was then that Zendaya said she understood what was going on.
“I was like, ‘Stop right now! You’re joking!’” she told the AP.

The film, based on Homer’s Ancient Greek epic poem of the same name, features a star-studded cast that includes Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, John Leguizamo, Lupita Nyong’o, Samantha Norton and Charlize Theron. It’s slated to hit theaters on July 17.
Zendaya told the AP that Holland’s delivery was “really cool.”

“He was ... allowed to be the one to tell me, and that was really special,” said Zendaya, who explained that she had already been overjoyed by Holland’s casting in the film. “I was already on cloud nine. The fact that I was even got to be involved as well was like just this cherry on top.”
The role certainly worked out for the actress. In an interview with TODAY, Nolan said that he was impressed with Zendaya, who he “often referred to on set as ‘perfect.’”
“To the chagrin of other people in the cast,” the director told TODAY correspondent Kaylee Hartung.
Matt Damon, who plays titular character Odysseus, and Holland said they were surprised by the director, who’s known for his analytical directing style and minimal notes to his actors.
“Shock and awe,” Holland said of his reaction.

title: Robert Irwin Shares Secret To Earning ‘Cool Points’ With Niece Grace, Daughter Of Bindi Irwin
summary: Robert Irwin said in an interview that his dance skills have earned him some “cool points” with his niece Grace, the daughter of Bindi Irwin.
story: Robert Irwin has found the key to his young niece’s heart.

Irwin told E! News in an interview on July 11 that he’s been able to connect with niece Grace Warrior Irwin Powell, the daughter of his sister Bindi Irwin and her husband Chandler Powell, through dance.

Irwin — who’s the host of upcoming  “Dancing with the Stars: The Next Pro,” a spinoff of the reality dance competition “Dancing with the Stars” of which he was a winner — said his skills have certainly come in handy.
“Uncle Robert has earned some further cool points because now I can teach Grace how to dance,” the 22-year-old told the outlet of his niece, who’s 5 years old. “She’s very happy about that.”

Irwin, a conservationist and son of the late Steve Irwin, told E! News that he’s had the opportunity to spend more quality time with Grace, whom he “loves with all my heart.” After all, the upcoming show, which airs on Monday, July 13, was filmed in Brisbane, Australia, just about an hour from where he and his family live.

“Every day I get back from shooting and Grace, my little niece, is like, ‘OK, teach me how to do the jive. Teach me how to do the tango,’” Irwin told the outlet. “She’s very little, so it’s a little bit challenging, but she’s such a bright and happy kid.”
Irwin, who said that his uncle duties are the “best job” he’s ever had, has not only made a name for himself in conservation, but also in the dance world.

Irwin was crowned the winner of “DWTS” Season 25 in November after a dominant run on the show. He cemented his status as a fan favorite from his very first dance, in which he performed a jungle-themed jive. His skills clearly run in the family as his sister also took home the reality show’s Mirrorball Trophy in 2015.
For the upcoming spinoff, Irwin won’t be competing — and in some ways, that’s a relief, he told ABC’s “Good Morning America.”

“I feel like going from contestant to host, first of all, I’m not getting judged, so that’s great. The other thing is, also, I feel like I can be, in some way, a bit of a mentor, because I’m obviously not the best dancer, but I had the best partner, I had Witney Carson,” Irwin said, referring to his “DWTS” partner and choreographer. “So, I know what it is to have a great pro partner teaching me ... I can say to these hopefuls, ‘Hey, this is what it takes.’”

title: Margaret Qualley Speaks Out After Reports of Jack Antonoff Split, Denies Infidelity Rumors
summary: A representative for Margaret Qualley slammed reports of the actor’s split from musician Jack Antonoff, after the Bleachers frontman was spotted attending Taylor Swift’s recent wedding alone.
story: A representative for Margaret Qualley slammed reports of the actor’s split from musician Jack Antonoff, after the Bleachers frontman was spotted attending Taylor Swift’s recent wedding alone.
In a statement shared with NBC News on July 10, Qualley’s rep said that the “narratives running in the press about Margaret and Jack are categorically untrue.”
Qualley’s camp also denied speculation of cheating in the couple’s marriage.

“There are no trust issues. There was no infidelity or anything outside of respect and partnership in this relationship,” the representative said in the statement about the couple, who have been married since August 2023. “They have deep love and care for one another.”

Antonoff, 42, was photographed alone while heading to New York’s Madison Square Garden for the July 3 wedding of close friend and collaborator Swift. Soon after, reports  began to circulate that the he and Qualley, 31, had separated. Some fans also noticed that photos of the couple’s wedding had been removed from Qualley’s Instagram page. And many others pointed out that her Instagram handle — which had previously been @isimostar, a reference to the Bleachers song “Isimo,”— had been changed in April to @sarahmargaretqualley23.
Qualley’s rep cautioned against believing the speculation, saying in the statement that “there are only two people in this marriage.”
“The sources who are talking to the press and commenting on their relationship are not people who know them,” the representative said in the statement. “Please respect their privacy.”

The pair were first linked in August 2021 after they were spotted kissing in Brooklyn. Months later, they attended the 2022 Critics Choice Awards, where Qualley was nominated for her performance in limited series “Maid.”  They were seen together again at the Grammys that same year, when Antonoff took home the producer of the year award.
At their 2023 wedding in New Jersey, the pair packed the house with a list of star-studded guests that included Swift, Lana Del Ray, Channing Tatum and Zoë Kravitz.

title: Meet the Cast of ‘Big Brother’ 2026: Who’s in Season 28?
summary: “Big Brother” has announced the houseguests for its upcoming Season 28. Meet the cast.
story: “Big Brother” fans, summer has officially arrived, which means it is time to meet the houseguests you’ll watch face the unexpected and compete for the next few months.

On July 7, “Big Brother” announced its Season 28 cast in a YouTube “Broveal” where fans watched a brief house tour before being introduced to the houseguests. Among the 14 contestants ready to form alliances, win Power of Vetoes and deceive are a rocket scientist, a MMA fighter and a “RuPaul’s Drag Race All Stars” alum.
The video began with host Julie Chen Moonves giving a sneak peek of the house.

“For Season 28, we’re throwing out all the rules of time and space and sending our houseguests on a journey unlike anything you’ve ever seen before,” Chen Moonves said. “History is about to be made. So buckle up, because we’re about to travel through time.”

She explained that time, including time travel, will be the theme for Season 28. After pointing out details in the living room, kitchen, lounge and more spots, it was time for the 14 houseguests to make an appearance. Each player mapped out some of their strategies and teased what viewers can expect from them.

But they are not the only players moving into the “Big Brother” house this season. CBS confirmed in a press release that more houseguests will be revealed during the show’s 90-minute premiere on Thursday, July 9, at 8 p.m. ET/ PT. The episode will also stream on Paramount+.

Two of the extra houseguests have already been revealed, one a reality television fan favorite and the other a “Big Brother” alum. “Survivor” Season 50 star Rick Devens will compete this season, Entertainment Weekly reported July 7. The publication also said that a second “Survivor” castaway will be joining Devens in the house.
Devens originally competed on “Survivor: Edge of Extinction” before returning for the historic Season 50 that aired earlier this year.

Angela Murray, who competed on “Big Brother” Season 26, will make her return, according to Men’s Journal. The Utah real estate agent was evicted in sixth place, delighting and frustrating fans with her chaotic gameplay. She also was a contestant on “The Amazing Race” Season 38, where she competed with her daughter Lexi.

Then during the “Big Brother: Unlocked” episode on July 10. The final houseguest of the season was revealed. After a fake-out during the premiere that showed “Big Brother” legend Rachel Reilly getting attacked by a velociraptor and falling into a volcano, she was replaced by “Survivor” Season 45 winner Dee Valladares.
Valladares said in the episode that she was looking forward to being the first-ever “Big Brother” and “Survivor” winner. She also knows Devens as the two both competed on “Survivor” Season 50.
What can Devens, Murray Valladares and the rest of houseguests expect this “Big Brother” season?

A press release for Season 28 reads, “This new group of houseguests is stepping into a summer where nothing is as it seems, where every twist rewrites the rules, and where time becomes the ultimate twist.”

Following the premiere, fans will get to see how the other additional houseguests disrupt the game when the “Big Brother Live Feeds,” which show the players in real time 24/7, begin on Friday, July 10, at 9 p.m. ET/ 6 p.m. PT on Paramount+ and Pluto TV. title: Lionel Messi Once Bathed Baby Lamine Yamal. Now, They Could Face Off In the World Cup
summary: Argentina star Lionel Messi once bathed a baby Lamine Yamal. Now, the two soccer superstars could face each other during the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
story: Of all the full-circle moments in sports history, this one might actually take the cake.

Argentinian soccer icon Lionel Messi was photographed in 2007 bathing an adorable, chubby baby as part of a charity calendar for his then-club FC Barcelona. Almost two decades later, Argentina is slated to move forward to the World Cup quarterfinals — and Messi might actually face off against that very child, Lamine Yamal, who grew up to be a superstar right winger for Spain.

Fans can’t get enough of the now-legendary throwback photo, with some saying that the baby bath was Messi’s “sacred” way of passing along his exceptional soccer prowess. Even comedian Trevor Noah has geeked out over the image.

“It’s crazy that it’s real. Imagine this moment,” Noah recently said during his World Cup Watch Party. “These people are both playing in the same World Cup right now. And this baby boy is one of the most talented players.”

Spain and Argentina, who are both headed to the Round of 8, are on opposite sides of the World Cup bracket, meaning Messi and Yamal wouldn’t face off on the pitch unless both teams make it to the finals.

Messi’s Team Argentina won 3-2 against Egypt on July 7. The 39-year-old, who missed a first-half penalty, made it up to his team with a goal, making him the first player in the contest’s history to score in six consecutive knockout-stage matches. Yamal, 18, is also lighting up the pitch, scoring just 10 minutes into his first World Cup start against Saudi Arabia on June 21. Spain most recently eliminated Belgium with a score of 2-0 on July 10.
The Story Behind Lionel Messi Bathing a Baby Lamine Yamal

Nineteen years before the two were tearing up the global stage, then-20-year-old Messi was holding a sudsy, 5-month-old Yamal in a baby basin. In the series of photos, Messi bathes the soapy baby. In one shot, Yamal’s mother, Sheila Ebana, assists Messi with the bath. In another photo, a smiling Messi cradles Yamal, who is wrapped in a towel.
Joan Monfort, then a freelance photographer for the Associated Press, told the Athletic in a 2024 interview that the meeting between the two would-be soccer stars was kismet.
“Back then, nobody could imagine that this baby would be who he is now — and you could not have known that Messi would become who he became, either,” Monfort said.
He added: “We are talking about 2007. Messi was only beginning at Barca then. Destiny plays an important role in these things.”

Monfort recalled to the Associated Press in 2024 that the shoot was part of an annual charity drive hosted by humanitarian aid organization UNICEF and local Barcelona sports outlet Diario Sport. He told the outlet that the organization had hosted a raffle, inviting those in the Rocafonda neighborhood in the Spanish city of Mataró to enter for a chance to have their picture taken at the iconic FC Barcelona stadium Camp Nou with a player. Yamal’s family just so happened to have won, Monfort said.
At the time, Messi wasn’t quite comfortable with handling baby Yamal, Monfort recalled to the AP.

“Messi is a pretty introverted guy, he’s shy,” Monfort told the outlet. “He was coming out of the locker room and suddenly he finds himself in another locker room with a plastic tub full of water and a baby in it. It was complicated. He didn’t even know how to hold him at first.”
But, as Monfort told the Athletic, Messi got more comfortable with the assignment.
“At the start, there was not much interaction,” he told the outlet. “It was difficult for all of them. But, bit by bit, it started to happen and in the end, it’s a pretty good photo.”

Astonishingly, Monfort said he wasn’t aware that the young child in the photos was, in fact, Yamal until a former colleague notified him that the snaps were going viral during the UEFA European Championship tournament in 2024, which was won by Spain. Yamal, then just 16 years old, had made a name for himself during that contest as the youngest player to not only appear in the tournament but also score. And it was during that tournament that Yamal’s father, Mounir Nasraoui, shared a bit about the photo’s backstory on his social media page.

“He told me the father had put it on social media,” Monfort previously told The Athletic of his colleague at Diario Sport. “In Sport, they could hardly believe it. They had just realized, too. It’s been really surprising, all this.”

For many fans, the photo has become evidence of a cosmic connection between the two players. And indeed, the similarities between Yamal and Messi continue to grow. Yamal, who made his debut in 2023, did so with none other than FC Barcelona, the team with which Messi had cemented his own name in soccer history. And since, Yamal has been recognized as somewhat of a successor to the Argentinian soccer icon, with fans saying that the rising star has restored some of the team’s dominant energy that Messi once brought.
“After Lionel Messi, he is our best player,” Barcelona midfielder Pablo Páez Gavira, known mononymously as Gavi, said.

title: Kandi Burruss’ Daughter, Riley, Shares How Parents’ Divorce Impacted Her
summary: Riley Burruss, Kandi Burruss’ daughter, opens up about how her mom’s recent split from stepdad Todd Tucker affected her.
story: Riley Burruss, daughter of singer-songwriter and “The Real Housewives of Atlanta” alum Kandi Burruss, is opening up about how she has been impacted by her mom’s recent split from stepdad Todd Tucker.
In November 2025, Kandi Burruss confirmed in a statement to People that she was separating from Tucker, whom she married in 2014. The magazine reported that the divorce was finalized in March.
Riley Burruss appeared as a guest on TODAY Radio Show on SiriusXM and shared how she has been feeling since the break up.

“I will say, a lot of people forget the fact that yes, a divorce happens between two people, but it affects more than just those two people,” she told host and TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle executive producer Talia Parkinson-Jones in a July 10 clip. “So it is really hard for me.”
She said that she has been struggling recently while shooting her Bravo series “Next Gen NYC” because she first learned about her mom and stepdad separating during filming.
“It’s just been a year of adapting,” she continued. “It’s tough at times. It’s easy at times. It’s confusing. I’m still learning, honestly.”

Parkinson-Jones said she could relate to Riley Burruss because she went through a similar situation when she was younger. She asked the reality television star what she has learned about her mother as they navigate this challenging time.

The 23-year-old replied, “I’ve learned from my mom that there are a lot of things that she protects in herself, and how strong she is, how courageous. Because all of this stuff, I didn’t even know. She wants to protect me the most she can. So being able to do that for your children, I think, is just a powerful thing.”
In her initial statement to People about her divorce, Kandi Burruss told the outlet that it had been “a difficult and emotional time.”

“After deep thought and a lot of prayer, I’ve made the decision to move forward with a divorce,” she said in a statement. “This is a difficult and emotional time, but my focus remains on protecting my peace, being the best mother I can be, and co-parenting with love and respect.”
She added that she was entering “a new chapter” in her life and focusing on her work, family and personal growth.
Part of that next chapter was starring on Broadway in the production of “& Juliet.” Burruss portrayed Angélique from December 11, 2025 to March 8.

During that run, she stopped by TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle to chat about the changes in her life. Jenna Bush Hager asked Kandi Burruss how co-parenting was going after pointing out that the Xscape singer spent the holidays with Tucker.

“Well, we have determined that no matter what, we’re always gonna be great co-parents for our kids. So that means that we’re going to spend holidays together sometimes because we’re still family, even though he and I have decided to go our separate ways,” Kandi Burruss responded.
She shared that she and her now ex-husband are “trying to make it as easy as possible for our children.”
Kandi Burruss told Sheinelle Jones that her Broadway show and many other projects were helping her cope.

“When I decided to do this show was right… in the thick of it,” she recalled. “So it has been the best therapy for me, because sometimes you have to have something to put your focus into or your attention, to keep your mind out of a sad place.”
The Grammy winner said that singing, performing and working out were her methods of healing.

“(I) do everything that I’m supposed to do to make sure I’m the best I can be on stage in front of everybody. While behind the scenes, I might be breaking down, but I have to keep it together and get it. It gives me motivation,” she explained.

Kandi Burruss shares 10-year-old son Ace and 6-year-old daughter Blaze with Tucker. She shares Riley Burruss with ex Russell “Block” Spencer. Tucker is also a dad to 30-year-old daughter Kaela Tucker, whom he welcomed during his relationship with ex Keema Parker.

title: This Is How Much Taylor Swift Paid Back NYC For Wedding Security
summary: Taylor Swift has paid back New York City for security and other costs tied to her lavish dayslong Madison Square Garden wedding festivities the week of July 4, according to Mayor Zohran Mamdani.
story: Singer Taylor Swift has paid back New York City for security and other costs tied to her lavish dayslong Madison Square Garden wedding festivities the week of July 4, the city’s mayor said.
Zohran Mamdani said in a press conference on July 10 that Swift has already shelled out more than $160,000 to cover public resources spent by the city.

“Taylor Swift … has paid already the cost of the permit that was lodged, which was over $160,000 for that event and for the response to that event,” Mamdani said, referencing her star-studded wedding. “That was a permit that was finalized, I think, in just the days before the event itself.”
Neither the NYPD nor Swift immediately responded to TODAY.com’s request for comment.

Mamdani’s comments come after criticisms around Swift and partner Travis Kelce’s use of taxpayer funds for their wedding. NBC News had confirmed that a permit was filed in the city for a major event at the legendary arena from July 2 through July 4, just ahead of the nuptials. Additionally, the outlet confirmed a New York Times report that an internal planning memo, distributed by the NYPD before the wedding, detailed the event’s security measures, including hundreds of officers scheduled to be on patrol.
The extra security measures drew the ire of many, including Republican congressmember Nicole Malliotakis of New York’s 11th Congressional District.

“Taylor Swift & Travis Kelce should reimburse NYPD for the 130 officers needed per day to keep their multi-million dollar, thousand person wedding at MSG safe,” Malliotakis wrote. “Our officers are already working overtime for 4th of July festivities & NYC taxpayers should NOT be on the hook.”

During the press conference, Mamdani acknowledged that the summer had been an eventful one for New York, with the city not only hosting Swift’s wedding, but also the Knicks’ first championship in 53 years, the World Cup and more.

title: McDonald’s Teams Up With BTS Again for BT21 Happy Meal: See the Toys
summary: McDonald’s latest collab with Jungkook, V, Jimin, Suga, Jin, RM and J-Hope enters the BT21 Universe, the collaborative project between BTS and Line Friends.
story: A toy chest full of uniquely “Dynamite” characters has arrived at McDonald’s.
The fast-food giant announced via its Menu Spotter that its latest BTS collab — the BT21 Happy Meal — will arrive at participating McDonald’s restaurants nationwide on July 14 for a limited time.
The chain’s newest partnership with Jungkook, V, Jimin, Suga, Jin, RM and J-Hope enters the BT21 Universe, the collaborative project between BTS and cuddly character platform Line Friends.

Customers who order a BT21 Happy Meal will receive one of 10 unique BT21 character toys with a ring clip, so folks can “hook TATA to your purse, put CHIMMY on RMyour keyring, or take the whole group of universtars with you on your backpack,” according to McDonald’s.

And there is more to explore on HappyMeal.com if you scan the QR code on your Happy Meal box. Customers can create different tracks and “bring their performance to life” alongside their favorite characters.

For folks unfamiliar with the BT21 Universe, KOYA, RJ, SHOOKY, MANG, CHIMMY, TATA, COOKY and VAN are friends who journey through outer space together. Seven of the eight characters symbolize members of BTS, and VAN, the guardian robot, represents the BTS Army.

Each BT21 character has elements of the performers’ personalities. For example, Jungkook’s BT21 character COOKY is “always full of heart and boundless stamina,” according to the BT21 website, while RM’s KOYA is the “sleeping cutie” who “naps with a mind heavily filled with thoughts.”

The Golden Arches has teamed up with the South Korean boy band a couple times in the past. In 2021, it dropped the BTS Meal, which featured a 10-piece Chicken McNuggets with Sweet Chili and Cajun dipping sauces inspired by McDonald’s South Korea, fries and a drink. The limited-time promotion was available in nearly 50 markets around the world.
A few years later, in September 2025, the chain tapped the “Butter” singers again to offer a Happy Meal special featuring two sets of TinyTAN toys inspired by each member of the group.

title: Meet the Cast of the New ‘Little House,’ and See How They Compare to the Original
summary: See how the cast of Netflix’s Little House on the Prairie compares to the original. Here are pictures of Ma, Pa, Laura and Mary.
story: Netflix is breathing new life into a beloved book and TV series.
On July 9, the streaming service debuted a reboot of “Little House on the Prairie,” the 1970s TV series that was based on a series of nine books by Laura Ingalls Wilder.
“Little House on the Prairie,” the third book in the series, inspired the name of the TV show.
Ingalls Wilder published the first book in the series, “Little House in the Big Woods,” in 1932. The entire series was inspired by her childhood growing up on the American frontier.
Netflix describes the reboot as “a transformed adaptation” that mixes “family drama” with an “epic survival tale” and an “origin story of the American West.”
As a new generation of viewers begins to follow the Ingalls family’s captivating story, we’re sharing more details on the actors who are stepping into the shoes of the original cast members.
Pa (Michael Landon and Luke Bracey)
In the original “Little House on the Prairie” TV series, Michael Landon played the role of Laura’s father, Charles Ingalls.

Affectionately called Pa, the character was known as a family man who wanted to seek a better life for his wife and daughters. Pa was a hardworking man, but he also found time for fun, and his fiddling skills were pretty impressive.
Throughout his acting career, Landon, who died in 1991, starred in several additional well-known roles as he appeared in “Bonanza” and “Highway to Heaven.”
In the reboot series, Luke Bracey steps into the role of Pa. Viewers may recognize the Australian actor from his roles in “Elvis,” “Hacksaw Ridge” and “Little Fires Everywhere.”
Bracey told Netflix’s Tudum he’d never read Ingalls Wilder’s books or watched the original TV series before becoming involved in the reboot.
“I found the audition quite difficult because I didn’t have any context of the tone of the show or what it was about,” he said. “I just took a stab in the dark.”
The TV series’ executive producer Joy Gorman Wettels told Tudum Bracey caught the casting team’s attention for a special reason.

“We were looking for someone who wasn’t only strapping and handsome and had that heart people expect from Michael Landon, but who also had a fresh perspective on what it meant to be a man in history,” she said. “Luke brought that.”
Ma (Karen Grassle and Crosby Fitzgerald)

“Little House on the Prairie” viewers will recall Laura’s mother, Caroline Ingalls (aka Ma), as being a loving and patient maternal figure. Alongside her husband, Ma played a pivotal role in shepherding her family to a new life in the West.
Karen Grassle originally played the role of Ma and nailed the balancing act of being strong, yet soft. The actor was also known for roles in “Not to Forget” and “Wyatt Earp.”
Crosby Fitzgerald is taking over for Grassle in the reboot series. The actor has appeared in “Crime 101,” “Palm Royale” and “The Twisted Tale of Amanda Knox.”
While speaking with Tudum, Fitzgerald admitted that the role of Caroline Ingalls was “a little bit daunting.”
“It’s my biggest role ever,” she said. “Also, I’ve never had a love interest.”
Luckily, Bracey helped Fitzgerald feel comfortable in the big shoes she was filling.
“He just immediately came with such a big heart and (was) such a safe place,” she said.
Laura (Melissa Gilbert and Alice Halsey)

“Little House on the Prairie” made Melissa Gilbert a household name. The young actor took on the role of Laura, a young girl who’s balancing childhood with change as her family uproots their life. Pa often called Laura “Half-Pint,” a sweet nickname he used to refer to her short stature.

Throughout her career, Gilbert has remain closely tied to the TV series. She’s also appeared in several other projects, including “Batman: The Animated Series,” “The Miracle Worker” and “Switched at Birth.”
In the reboot, Alice Halsey tries her hand at portraying the iconic character. In an interview with Tudum, the young actor says Laura “inspires” her.
“She’s very sure of herself. She’s very confident. And I think that benefits her throughout her entire story,” she said.
Viewers may have seen Halsey in “Lessons in Chemistry” and “Days of Our Lives” previously.
Rebecca Sonnenshine, the creator of the first season of the reboot, told Tudum that Halsey stood out while the team was casting the role of Laura.
“There’s a boldness about her, a forthrightness, a natural curiosity that comes across in her performance and in her personality that really captures who Laura was,” she said.
Mary (Melissa Sue Anderson and Skywalker Hughes)
Melissa Sue Anderson played the role of Mary, Laura’s older sister, in the original “Little House on the Prairie” TV series.

Quiet and studious, Mary was close to Laura, despite being utterly different from her sister. For this reason, they often clashed. One of the character’s most memorable storylines occurred in the original series when Mary went blind.
In addition to appearing in the iconic series, Anderson was also known for her roles in “Happy Birthday to Me” and “Midnight Offerings.”
Now, Skywalker Hughes is playing the role of Mary in the reboot series. In an interview with Tudum, the young actor said she was thrilled to portray a character she already knew quite well.
“I grew up with the books on my bedside table since I was itsy-bitsy, and I would always get my mom to read them to me!” she said.
Viewers may have seen the young actor in “I, Object” and “Joe PIckett.”

title: ‘Married at First Sight’ Exclusive: Groom Only Has 1 Word for the Woman He’s About to Marry
summary: Felipe Cruz is shocked by bride Tori Dahl in the Married at First Sight Season 20 premiere. See a first look at the moment.
story: Wedding jitters are expected at the altar. But when Felipe Cruz saw his bride, Tori Dahl, walking toward him, there was even more reason to be nervous.

Cruz, 29, and Dahl, 32, had never met before. In TODAY.com’s exclusive first look at the upcoming season of “Married at First Sight,” airing on Peacock on July 12, the pair meets for the first time moments before saying “I do” — and Cruz’s reaction to seeing his soon-to-be-wife says it all.
“Wow!” He exclaimed, laughing.
After the couple officially introduced themselves, he immediately complimented his glamorous bride: “Tori, you are stunning.”
She thanked him, but kept her focus on the reason they were there: getting married.
“Let’s do this,” she said.
Cruz agreed: “Let’s do this.”

With the help of relationship experts, the long-running reality series sets up strangers to get married without ever having met before. In its 20th season, and the franchise’s first on Peacock, seven Seattle-based couples are guided through the trials and tribulations of marriage as they hope to find love. The track record isn’t always the best, as Season 19 shows, but the series has produced some long-lasting couples.
For Dahl and Cruz, Peacock’s full-length trailer hints that the road after the altar may not be too smooth.

“If I were a betting man, and I had to, let’s just say, pick people that I don’t think are going to work out, it’d be Felipe. No question about it,” said fellow participant Nick Unlenhuth, after Dahl told the other men that he had cheated once in the past.

Whether Unlenhuth’s warning proves right remains to be seen. For now, Cruz and Dahl’s story begins with a seemingly happy surprise at the altar — but whether that first spark can turn into everlasting love is exactly what the extreme “Married at First Sight” experiment is designed to find out.

title: Anne Hathaway and Zendaya Both Earned 1 Word of Rare Praise From Christopher Nolan (and Matt Damon Never Did)
summary: Here’s the one word Christopher Nolan told Anne Hathaway and Zendaya.
story: Christopher Nolan handpicked some of Hollywood’s hottest actors — including Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, John Leguizamo, Lupita Nyong’o, Samantha Norton, Zendaya and Charlize Theron — to star in his upcoming action movie “The Odyssey,” in theaters July 17.
The movie, which is based on the ancient Greek writer Homer’s epic poem about the aftermath of the Trojan War, stars Oscar winner Damon as the Greek king Odysseus, and Holland as his son Telemachus.

But it was Nolan’s rare praise for Zendaya and Hathaway during shooting of the movie that sparked a friendly on-set rivalry among cast members, the director and his stars told TODAY correspondent Kaylee Hartung.
During filming, Nolan, who’s known for his analytical directing style, which includes minimal notes to his actors, was admittedly wowed by Zendaya’s performance as the Greek goddess Athena.
“Often referred to on set as perfect,” Nolan said of Zendaya.
“To the chagrin of other people in the cast,” the director added, laughing.
“Sorry, guys,” Zendaya joked to the others.
“Still recovering,” quipped Damon.
“It’s a touchy subject,” Zendaya added.
Were the rumors true that Nolan decided that Zendaya’s performance was “perfect” after her first take?
“I don’t know if it was the first,” Zendaya responded, laughing.
“I felt incredibly encouraged,” she added of the director’s feedback.
Damon and Holland recalled hearing Nolan’s effusive praise for Zendaya. Their reaction?
“Shock and awe,” Holland said to laughter.
Oscar winner Hathaway’s performance as Penelope, Odysseus’s wife, also earned the director’s adulation.
“I think Anne may have gotten a ‘perfect’ actually,” Holland recalled.
“I did,” Hathaway said, adding, “I wrote about it in my journal.”
Though some cast members hadn’t read Homer’s poem prior to being cast, Hathaway was already a fan.
“I did, like, yelp and shriek when Chris said it was ‘The Odyssey.’ It was not a very low-key reaction. I was not calm,” said Hathaway.
Zendaya’s role in the “The Odyssey,” which marks her first collaboration with Nolan, came as a surprise, she said.
Zendaya learned she would appear in the movie after Holland, her “Spider-Man” franchise co-star and now-husband , was already cast.
“It was funny because when he got the call I was just over the moon for him. Like, my heart was so full,” Zendaya said.
“I was just excited about this journey that you were going go on,” she told Holland, “and really didn’t kind of put myself into that equation at all.”
“So it was quite a pleasant surprise,” she said.

title: Francis Ford Coppola Shares Moving Post About Friend Danny Glover After the Actor’s Alzheimer’s Diagnosis
summary: Francis Ford Coppola, 87, posted some words of support on social media for Danny Glover, who had recently shared that he had been living with Alzheimer’s for several years.
story: Francis Ford Coppola is sharing some words of support for an old friend.

The 87-year-old director took to social media on July 8 to express his solidarity with legendary actor Danny Glover, who told TODAY in an exclusive interview that he has been living with Alzheimer’s disease for multiple years.
Coppola reflected on how the actor, who worked with the director on his 1997 film “The Rainmaker,” was a stand up guy.

Glover was “a most wonderful cast member: considerate of the others, kind and supportive, always available to help out, run lines with the others even when not scheduled,” Coppola wrote on social media. “He was a terrific cast member and I became so fond of him and of course am disturbed that he is suffering now.”
Coppola added: “Danny may have difficulty remembering, but those who know and love him can’t forget.”

In the legal drama film, which was also written by Coppola, Glover played the empathetic Judge Tyrone Kipler. While Glover was uncredited in the movie, he still managed to draw praise for his portrayal, including a 1998 NAACP Image Award nomination for best supporting actor in a motion picture.
Coppola’s moving message elicited a deluge of responses from fans, including other actors who gushed over their experiences working with Glover.
“He is the greatest guy to work with,” said Cary Elwes, who appeared alongside the iconic actor in 2004’s “Saw.” “So sad that he is going through this 🙏”
Filmmaker Deon Taylor commented on the post, calling on fans to give Glover “all the flowers he deserves.”
“His willingness to fight for his people and stand when others were afraid makes him more impactful than words can explain!” Taylor wrote.
While Glover has been living with the neurodegenerative disease for years, he told TODAY that he felt it was time to go public with the news.
“I’m sure as it advances, things are going to be different and changing,” Glover said.

The four-time Emmy winning actor explained that since his diagnosis, his movements, speech and memories have slowed. He’s continued to remain active, however, attending events and interacting with community members in San Francisco, where he lives. His daughter Mandisa underscored in the interview that it’s important for the actor to maintain “control of his own narrative, of his own life story.”
“The time is now,” she said. “What better time but now for him to speak for himself?”

title: Beauty Influencer Is Embracing Comments About Erling Haaland Resemblance: ‘Fabulous Hair’
summary: After a content creator Emma Willman went viral for her likeness to Norwegian soccer star Erling Haaland, she leaned into the moment, re-creating some of this most iconic hairstyles.
story: After a content creator went viral for her likeness to Norwegian soccer star Erling Haaland, she leaned into the moment in a way that would’ve made The Lions proud.

Emma Willman, a South Carolina-based influencer who specializes in hair and beauty content, has been re-creating a number of Haaland’s iconic looks, including his golden double braids and signature, slicked-back bun. The Haaland-inspired hair tutorials come after the 24-year-old posted a viral french braid “how-to” video in early June. It drew more than 1.3 million likes and 181,000 comments from not only hair enthusiasts and dedicated soccer fans, but soccer brands and the World Cup fan favorite himself. Score!
When it comes to the deluge of doppelgänger comments, Willman tells TODAY.com that she’s lovin’ it.

“It’s been so fun to see — especially to see all the fans in the comments. He’s definitely someone who has a lot of fun with what he does,” Willman says of the 25-year-old striker, who’s become a highly-memed internet fan-favorite for his antics both on and off the pitch. “I think it’s really special that I’m able to do the same thing.”

In her viral video, Willman shares simple, step-by-step instructions on how to french braid, parting her hair down the middle and effortlessly twisting strands into the finished look. Willman says that while she’s sporadically received quips about her resemblance to the Manchester City player, it wasn’t until the french braid video began circulating amid the World Cup tournament that the comparison really took off. And social media users couldn’t help themselves from pointing out what they felt was obvious.

“For as long as I’ve been on social media, a lot of people would make the comment here or there that I did resemble him, but it wasn’t to the point where I would say I really noticed,” Willman says. “I guess because of how well he’s playing and everything going on right now, I woke up and literally my video had went insanely viral overnight.”

Haaland — who scored two game-winning goals against Brazil, sending the five-time World Cup champs home — greenlit the comparisons with a simple comment of “Hi👍🏻.” The greeting alone drew more than 2.3 million likes.
In a follow-up video from July 7, Willman re-creates Haaland’s bun and comes to terms with her celebrity lookalike.
“I’ll be so honest,” Willman says in the video. “I also see the resemblance.”
Haaland isn’t even the only big name who’s intrigued by the twinning. Brands got in on the action, too.
“There is nø way you two aren’t related,” Adidas wrote under one of Willman’s videos.
Modelo USA called on people to “check the family tree ASAP.”

Willman says that because Haaland is known for his “fabulous hair,” she’s been flattered by the comparisons. She adds that her newfound virality has been enjoyable, especially because she’s been able to learn more about the game, as well as about the striker and his fans.

“It’s been fun for me to play into it and get to know the fan base a little bit more, because that’s exactly what he would do,” Willman says. “He’s someone that I think everyone should look up to, especially with how well he’s playing and how he treats his reputation around the sport.”
The content creator says she’s headed to the England vs. Norway World Cup game on July 11 in Miami. And she’s hoping that she can finally meet her twin.

“I’m really excited about the trip and going to see the game in person and whatever is able to come from that,” Willman says. “If I did meet him, I think that that would probably be one of the highlights of my life.”
As for any hair tips that fans can use to get their own Haaland-ified locks, Willman recommends eating right, using rosemary hair oil and embracing your natural hair.

“I cannot compare my hair to as great as his is, of course,” Willman says with a laugh. “But I have been very big into embracing my natural hair lately … it’s so fun to have your natural hair texture out.”

title: ‘Moana’ Reviews: Here’s What Critics Are Saying About the Live-Action Movie
summary: What are critics saying about Moana? Read reviews and whether the movie was worth a remake.
story: “Moana” returns 11 years after the animated musical first premiered, this time as a live-action movie.
Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson reprises his role as the Polynesian demigod Maui alongside Catherine Laga’aia as Moana in her film debut.

Critics are split over the new “Moana,” with some saying the movie stands alone and others calling its scene-for-scene resemblance to the 2016 film a “cash grab.” That said, most agree that Laga’aia made an impressive lead entrance into the beloved story.
Keep reading to see which critics find paradise in this live-action interpretation, and which wish they could stay in 2016.
Associated Press

For The Associated Press, Jake Coyle praises the story of Moana and her triumph to save her community, but feels as though the live-action take has even less of a purpose than the 2024 animated sequel, “Moana 2.”
He writes that the live-action film offers “little more than a lamentable swap of cartoon imagination for live-action do-over” and closer resembles a “Saturday Night Live” parody sketch.
Observing the scene-for-scene correspondence between the live-action film and its animated big sister, Coyle concludes, “All inventiveness has gone out to sea.”
While enjoying the performances, he still finds that “Moana is in increasingly desperate need of some new waters to explore.”
Variety
Writing for Variety, Owen Gleiberman says the movie “works 100%” and “soars” above the “blues” of other Disney live-action journeys.
A main reason for Gleiberman’s stance on “Moana,” he says, is the blend of live-action and computer-generated animation.

“There’s a ton of CG in the new ‘Moana’ that’s executed quite artfully, and that helps the director, Thomas Kail, create a buoyant atmosphere of visual vibrance,” Gleiberman writes. “It all establishes a free-flowing universe that exists halfway between live action and animation.”
After high praise for Johnson’s on-screen reprise of Maui and the timelessness of Lin-Manuel Miranda and Opetaia Foa’i’s score, Gleiberman says the remake indeed has value.
“The remake of ‘Moana’ can’t, and shouldn’t, replace the original,” he writes. “But it earns a place alongside it.”
Vulture
Critic Alison Willmore phrases her stance in two terse words for Vulture: “Please stop.”
She posits the movie’s goal is “to squeeze as much revenue as possible from the existing hits because the powers that be no longer have confidence in their ability to turn out new ones.”
Ultimately, Willmore sees no payoff for this film, which she says is “pulling the material to its breaking point.”
The Hollywood Reporter
David Rooney starts off his review for The Hollywood Reporter applauding the lead performances and praising the movie: “This charming new iteration stands confidently on its own.”

Although skeptical, like Willmore, of what seems to be a “cash grab” business strategy behind live-action projects, he sees the same chance for intergenerational connection in watching the “fresh sparkle on beloved material” with younger family.
“Does it bring new ideas to the material? No. Does that matter? Also no,” he writes.

title: How Levi’s Fostered a Connection with Beyoncè That Spans Decades — and Created a ‘Pinch Me’ Moment for Its CEO
summary: When Beyoncé named a song “Levii’s Jeans” and then spearheaded a buzzy ad campaign for Levi’s in 2024, it was more than just a “pinch me” moment for the company’s CEO.
story: When Beyoncé named a song “Levii’s Jeans” and then spearheaded a buzzy ad campaign for Levi’s in 2024, it was more than just a “pinch me” moment for the company’s CEO.
It was a symbol that the iconic brand is just as relevant today as when founder Levi Strauss began selling his jeans in San Francisco during the California Gold Rush in 1873.

“There are many ‘pinch me’ moments. We come in every day to do our best work around Levi’s and the brand, but when you take a step back, you realize that you are part of something that is bigger than ourselves,” Levi Strauss & Co. CEO Michelle Gass told NBC News correspondent Savannah Sellers for the NBC News series “Business in America.”

“It’s a brand that is one of the most beloved iconic brands in the world, and with that comes a tremendous amount of responsibility to lean in, to evolve, to honor that legacy, but not be constrained by it.”

Even for a company that has become synonymous with jeans and more during its long history, having one of the world’s biggest singers namecheck Levi’s in her 2024 song with Post Malone on her “Cowboy Carter” album was a moment to savor.
More of NBC’s ‘Business in America’

Barnes & Noble CEO Would Support Stores Selling AI-Written Books. Here’s WhyNike CEO Gave His Personal Email Address to Employees: ‘It’s Not a Job. It’s Personal’3 Tips from Zillow’s CEO That Can Help Your Home Sell Faster — and For More Money
Barnes & Noble CEO Would Support Stores Selling AI-Written Books. Here’s Why
Nike CEO Gave His Personal Email Address to Employees: ‘It’s Not a Job. It’s Personal’
3 Tips from Zillow’s CEO That Can Help Your Home Sell Faster — and For More Money

“When Beyoncé names a song after us, that doesn’t happen very often, right?” Gass said. “How many brands can say that they have a song named after them by one of the most celebrated artists of our time?”
Levi’s viewed the star’s song as a chance to work with her on a deeper level.

“That happened based on decades of a relationship with Beyoncé, so you know Levi’s and Beyoncé have connected way back since, like, the ‘90s when she was part of Destiny’s Child,” Gass said. “She’s shown up in 501 shorts at Coachella, and so there’s been this great relationship. She decides to name a song after us, and for many that could have been good enough.

“And I think for us, we just said, ‘Wow, well, that’s pretty powerful on its own, maybe it could lead to something bigger,’” she continued. “And we had a few conversations, and that led to a phenomenal campaign with Beyonce last year.”

Following a campaign that launched in 2024, a Levi’s commercial dropped a year later with Beyoncé arriving at a bar in her bedazzled Levi’s jeans and denim jacket. It fit the theme of her “Cowboy Carter” album and had fans buzzing.
Sellers was able to get an in-person look on TODAY at the blingy jeans the singer wore for the campaign.

“As you can see, these are 501 but it’s the 501 curve,” Gass said. “So one of the things we’ve been talking about is how we always respect our heritage. The 501 is the 501 that it has been for 150 years, but we’re constantly innovating and evolving, and so this is the 501 curve, which was designed out of the request for women to wear 501s but to fit a curvier body. And then, as you can see, of course, with Beyoncé, you see the embellishments, the crystals, the bling. So beautiful.”
Beyoncé is the latest American icon to be connected to the brand.

“We like to think about Levi’s as the unofficial uniform of progress,” Gass said. “And when you think about all of the people over generations. Whether you go back to even like a Marilyn Monroe or Elvis Presley, Steve Jobs, Beyoncé, you name it. You can name hundreds and hundreds of people who have worn Levi’s and done pretty incredible things.
“And it’s our responsibility, all of us working here to make sure that we preserve that. We really honor that legacy, but we carry it forward, so we stay relevant.”

In her wide-ranging conversation with Sellers, Gass also touched on how the company is implementing artificial intelligence among fears of job losses due to AI, Levi’s focus on increasing its reach among female consumers she believes are “underserved,” and the future of physical retail stores.

title: Jenna Bush Hager Was Shocked By Her ‘Five Star Weekend’ Cameo ... and Impressed!
summary: TODAY’s Jenna Bush-Hager, who makes a cameo in “The Five-Star Weekend,” a new Peacock series starring Jennifer Garner, dishes about her scene.
story: TODAY’s Jenna Bush-Hager, like so many others, is a huge fan of Elin Hilderbrand’s literary universe. Now, she’s made it onto the screen for a special cameo in “The Five Star Weekend,” the latest Hilderbrand title to leave the page and hit the screen.

“I was thrilled to be asked to be an extra in ‘The Five Star Weekend,’ not only because I love Elin Hilderbrand and I love this book, but also because, I mean, I’m co-starring with Jen Garner! The queen herself,” Jenna tells TODAY.com.

“The Five Star Weekend,” which is based on the 2023 novel and premiered on Peacock July 9, stars Jennifer Garner as Hollis Shaw, a famous cook who, when met with a heartbreaking personal loss, comes to terms with the navigation of grief and familial tension alongside the demanding spotlight of her high-profile career.
Jenna tells TODAY.com that she didn’t realize how important her minor, yet pivotal, guest role would be.
“I also didn’t know the extent of my part,” Jenna says. “It’s a pretty dramatic role, so I was proud of myself. I hung in there.”

In the premiere episode, Jenna plays herself and is cooking with Hollis during a TODAY segment. Hollis is promoting her second cookbook and chatting about the “family-favorite” roasted red onion dip they are making when Jenna asks how she can cut the onions without crying.
“Well, my husband just died so I can’t do anything without crying,” Hollis replies, processing her loved one’s tragic death live on air and breaking down in tears.
The moment sets up the rest of the season and why Hollis embarks on a girl’s trip to help her grieve.
Reflecting on the set’s atmosphere, Jenna says she felt welcomed into this beloved series. She also shares what fans of this novel can expect from watching.
“Jennifer Garner is the most gracious,” Jenna says. “And Elin Hilderbrand is the queen of not only the beach read but, I think you’ll soon see, the adaptation.”

Hilderbrand’s novel “Perfect Couple” was adapted into a successful Netflix series in 2024. Many of her other books, including her “Paradise” series, “28 Summers,” “The Hotel Nantucket” and “Winter Street” are also in development for adaptations across streaming platforms.
(Peacock and NBC are owned by NBCUniversal, TODAY’s parent company.)

title: U.S. insists Strait of Hormuz remains open despite Iran declaring it closed
summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened Iran after the funeral of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei saw open calls for his killing.
story: The United States launched another round of strikes against Iran overnight in retaliation for its attack on a Cyprus-flagged container ship in the Strait of Hormuz.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.
U.S. Central Command said Saturday night that the strikes were carried out at the behest of President Donald Trump.

Before the announcement, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps navy declared the disputed Strait of Hormuz closed, blaming foreign interference and attempts by several vessels to pass through unauthorized routes, as it said it struck one transiting ship.
Iran’s shuttering of the strait was not mentioned in the U.S. Central Command statement on the fresh strikes, which only mentioned the attack on the Cyprus-flagged vessel.
CENTCOM said a crew member is missing and the ship, the M/V GFS Galaxy, cannot continue its voyage after a fire and engine room damage.
“The United States is imposing a heavy cost by continuing to degrade Iran’s ability to attack civilian mariners and commercial ships freely transiting the strait,” it said in a statement.
Late Saturday, CENTCOM said the strikes had concluded and that U.S. forces hit 140 military targets, including Iranian missile and drone sites, naval capabilities and coastal surveillance locations.

CENTCOM insisted the Strait of Hormuz “is open to all vessels seeking to lawfully transit the international waterway,” adding: “U.S. forces are positioned and prepared to ensure that freedom of navigation remains available despite unwarranted Iranian aggression, harassment, threats, and arbitrary declarations. Iran does not control the strait. Traffic is flowing.”
Strait of Hormuz closed

The IRGC said earlier that the strait’s closure was the result of “insecurity created by the unlawful interference of foreign actors” and warned that any military strikes over the matter would be met with “a forceful response.”
“Additional enemy bases in the region will be targeted,” the IRGC said via official state news agency the Islamic Republic News Agency.
It later said it responded to American strikes, hitting military targets in Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar and Oman.
Ballistic missiles were fired at “important military infrastructure and facilities at Jordan’s Prince Hassan Air Base,” the IRGC said.
The strait, the key waterway that served as the route for roughly one-fifth the world’s oil supply before the war, has been a sore spot for Iran and the United States amid attempts to broker peace.

The IRGC said it had warned that “foreign interference and the unlawful designation of shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz would be met with a firm response and would disrupt the increasing flow of maritime traffic through the strait.”
It said that its military struck one vessel with warning fire and stopped it after it “switched off its tracking and identification systems, thereby endangering maritime security.”
“The Strait of Hormuz is closed until further notice and will remain closed until the end of U.S. interference in the region,” the IRGC said.
“No vessel will be permitted to transit the strait,” it said.
Khamenei pledges revenge
The rapid return to warlike stances took place in the wake of the burial of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed Feb. 28 in the opening strikes of the war, in the holy city of Mashhad.
Iran’s new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei pledged Sunday to take revenge for the death of his father.

“We pledge that we will take revenge for the pure blood of the martyred leader and all the martyrs of these two wars from the criminal and disgraced killers,” he said in a funeral message reported by Iranian state media.
“Revenge is the demand of our nation and must certainly be carried out,” he added. “Soon, the free people of the world will carry out a part of this divine mission.”

Mojtaba Khamenei, 56, was seriously wounded in the same attack that killed his father, sources previously told NBC News. Though Iranian officials have downplayed reports of his injuries, no photo or audio recording of him has been released.

The younger Khamenei, who has not been seen since the war began, did not attend any public events as part of his father’s  sprawling funeral ceremony that saw his body taken to five cities in both Iran and Iraq. The stateyea ment attributed to him, like all others issued in his name as supreme leader, was a written message.

The late supreme leader was laid to rest at the shrine of Imam Reza, Iran’s holiest Shia Muslim site on Thursday, marking the end of six days of public mourning ceremonies. Neither the U.S. nor Israel directly targeted funeral sites during the ceremonies.
Warning from Trump

President Trump earlier warned Iran against any attempts to assassinate him after Khamenei’s funeral saw numerous English-language banners openly calling for Trump to be killed along with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

A thousand missiles “are Locked and Loaded and aimed at the Islamic Republic of Iran, with thousands of more to immediately follow, should the Iranian Government act on its threat,” Trump wrote in the overnight post.
Trump said he had issued instructions to the U.S. military to follow in the event of his death, adding that they would “completely decimate and destroy all areas of Iran.”

He signed off the post “PRAISE BE TO ALLAH!” — an invocation the leader has repeatedly used during the war. The Council on American-Islamic Relations, a nationwide advocacy group, in the past has criticized Trump’s “deranged mocking of Islam.”
The threats against Trump have further underlined the tensions gripping the Middle East as an interim deal to end the war buckles under repeated crossfire in the region.

There had been multiple days of U.S. airstrikes targeting Iran, as well as Iranian retaliatory fire targeting nations across the region. Those strikes had been sparked by Iran attacking three ships in the strait earlier this week.
Foreign ministers meeting

Iran and Oman’s foreign ministers met on Saturday to discuss the Strait of Hormuz, which lies between them, after days of Iranian attacks on ships and U.S. retaliation that dealt a blow to the interim deal to end the war.

Oman said it and Iran agreed to keep talking about the crucial waterway “at the technical and political levels,” a day after the United States called on Iran to publicly say the crucial waterway is open and ships won’t be attacked.

Iran has said the strait must be under its sole control and that vessels should begin to pay fees to Tehran — even though the world for decades has considered it an international waterway. About a fifth of all traded oil and natural gas passed through the strait before the war began.
Iran’s grip on the strait during the conflict led to a global energy crisis, though oil prices have sharply dropped since wartime highs of $120 a barrel.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Saturday accused the U.S. of violating the interim deal by ending waivers allowing Iran to sell crude oil on the open market in U.S. dollars, which Washington did in response to the attacks on ships in the strait.
“Reality check: There can only be mutual compliance,” Araghchi wrote on X.

title: 2 killed, 6 injured at Toronto festival after pair of gunmen shoot at each other
summary: Two people were killed and three others were wounded in a shooting Saturday at the Salsa on St. Clair festival in Toronto, police said.
story: Two people were killed and six others were injured when a pair of gunmen opened fire at a festival celebrating Latino culture in Toronto on Saturday, police said.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

Two of the victims were pronounced dead at the scene, while five others suffered gunshot wounds and another was hospitalized with unspecified injuries following the gunfire in the area of St. Clair and Arlington avenues during the Salsa on St. Clair festival, Toronto police said.
“There seemed to be an exchange of gunfire between individuals targeting each other,” Frank Barredo, Toronto Police Service deputy chief, said during a news conference.
Four of the wounded were hospitalized with “serious” injuries, Barredo said.
It wasn’t clear whether the gunmen were among the dead or injured, nor could police say late Saturday whether any shooter was still being sought.
The shooting was reported around 8:12 p.m., Barredo said. An estimated 13,000 people were taking part in the festival, he said.
Two guns were recovered and investigators were focused on three different crime scenes, the chief said, adding that the investigation would be “complex.”
Mayor Olivia Chow expressed anger over the violence, especially because the festival attracts children and families.
“I’m deeply disturbed and angry about this reckless, irresponsible act of violence right in the middle of a festival,” she said at the news conference.
One witness, Pamela Garcia, told Toronto news outlet CP24 that she heard three shots and saw people in the crowd run and scream.
Another witness, Jacy Lin, recalled being at the festival’s salsa stage and seeing everyone suddenly run toward it before police arrived, the music stopped and people began leaving.

“I was walking from here and there was like a yellow tape, and I saw a bunch of paramedics coming down with a man and they were just doing CPR,” Lin said. “And he had like an oxygen tank and everything, and he didn’t look well.”
Salsa on St. Clair is a two-day festival celebrating Latino culture with music, dance food and art. It started Saturday and was set to run through Sunday on Toronto’s St. Clair Avenue.

title: U.S. and Iran exchange intense new attacks after Trump says ceasefire is ‘over’
summary: A U.S. official told NBC News the U.S. hadn’t carried out any further strikes Thursday, contradicting Iranian officials, though the military has been shooting down incoming Iranian projectiles.
story: The United States and Iran have traded new attacks, intensifying an exchange that threatens to collapse their agreement to end the war.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

The American military said it hit around 90 targets in airstrikes across Iran on Wednesday, after President Donald Trump said he considered the tenuous ceasefire between the two countries over following Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

Tehran retaliated with attacks on U.S. allies across the Middle East — a wave of strikes that sparked alerts in Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and hours later in Jordan — as the two sides accused each other of violating the terms of their interim deal.
The two days of renewed fighting cast doubt on whether Washington and Tehran remained committed to reaching a final deal to end the war, which was launched by the U.S. and Israel in February.

The U.S. military said Wednesday that it struck “approximately 90 Iranian military targets including air defense systems, coastal surveillance assets, missile and drone storage sites, naval capabilities, and military logistics infrastructure along Iran’s coastline.”

A U.S. official told NBC News that the U.S. had not carried out any further strikes on Thursday, contradicting Iranian officials, though the military has been shooting down incoming Iranian projectiles.
There are no reports of any injuries or significant damage to U.S. facilities, and the U.S. and allies shot down nearly all incoming threats, or they failed to reach targets, the official said.
Falling debris from interceptions did cause some damage, the official said, including to one non-U.S. building near the U.S. Navy headquarters in Bahrain.
The U.S. strikes on Wednesday targeted places that were allowing the IRGC to resupply locations and reconstitute their attacks, the official said.

But Iranian state media reported multiple explosions in cities across the country’s south, and the Foreign Ministry denounced Wednesday’s strikes as a “grave war crime,” saying they targeted civilian infrastructure including two railway bridges.

It said the bridges that were attacked lie on the route to Mashhad, where officials plan to bury the country’s slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Thursday. Videos geolocated by NBC News showed a damaged railway bridge in Golestan province, which is between Tehran and Mashhad.
The U.S. official on Thursday denied targeting the Bushehr nuclear power plant after a local official said an airstrike hit the perimeter of the plant, according to the state-run IRNA news agency.
At least 14 people were killed and another 78 wounded in the two days of U.S. attacks, the Iranian Health Ministry said Thursday in its first overall count of casualties.
There was no immediate response to the Iranian accusations from the Pentagon.

A similar exchange of attacks took place in late June, with an Iranian attack on a commercial ship in the Strait of Hormuz, followed by U.S. military strikes in and around the strait and retaliatory Iranian attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait.
This time, Iran’s retaliation also targeted Qatar and Jordan, the latter of which said it shot down eight Iranian missiles at around 7 a.m. ET Thursday.
The IRGC said it fired 10 ballistic missiles, targeting a U.S. command and control center, as well as an air base in Jordan.
The exchanges left the peace process in limbo. Trump and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding in mid-June, which kicked off a 60-day negotiating period toward a final deal to end the conflict.

Those talks have been paused this week as Iran holds massive funeral events for Khamenei, who was killed in U.S.-Israeli strikes at the start of the war. The funeral will culminate Thursday with a burial ceremony in Mashhad, his hometown and the site of the most prominent Shia shrine in Iran.

Trump, who wrapped up a NATO summit in Turkey on Wednesday, had signaled intense strikes were coming. “This is in retribution for yesterday’s bombing of ships by Iran. If it happens again, it will get much worse!” he warned.

The president dismissed the ongoing peace efforts and labeled Iranian leaders “scum,” but said he would allow negotiations to continue and did not think this new fighting would result in “long-term” military action.
Speaking with reporters later aboard Air Force One, Trump insisted that Iran was desperate to make a deal despite the recent escalation.
“I just don’t know that they’re worthy of making a deal,” he said. “I don’t know that they’re going to honor the deal. That’s the problem.”

Asked why Tehran would attack commercial vessels amid the ongoing ceasefire, Trump responded, “because they’re sort of crazy, to be honest with you. ... They’re a little bit out of control, but they wanna make a deal badly.”
The status of the Strait of Hormuz, through which some 20% of the world’s oil passed before the war, has become a major sticking point in talks.
Iran has insisted that it has a right to charge a fee for ships that pass through the strait, and it attacked ships in an apparent effort to assert its authority over the crucial waterway.
That ignited this new exchange of fire. But there may be few good options left for Trump, analysts say.

“His pessimism in not getting a final agreement, I think, is well placed, but that doesn’t mean that, you know, the no war, no agreement, no peace situation is also sustainable,” said Ali Vaez, Iran project director for the International Crisis Group think tank.
“He has to get into some kind of understanding with Iran, and there is no way that he would be able to renegotiate the MOU, so his only option is to get back to it.”

title: U.K. rattled by killing of politician Ann Widdecombe as murder probe continues
summary: LONDON — A former British lawmaker was found dead with serious injuries at her home Thursday, prompting a murder investigation that has reignited concerns about the safety of the country’s politicians.
story: LONDON — A former British lawmaker was found dead with serious injuries at her home Thursday, prompting a murder investigation that has reignited concerns about the safety of the country’s politicians.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

Ann Widdecombe, 78, was one of Britain’s most recognizable politicians, serving as a Conservative member of Parliament for two decades before reinventing herself as a television personality. Known for her strong socially conservative views on abortion and LGBTQ rights, she more recently served as justice spokesperson for the hard-right Reform UK party.
The death has renewed unease about the safety of Britain’s politicians after two others were killed in the last decade.

On Sunday, police said a 28-year-old man had been arrested in northern England on suspicion of murder, and had been taken into custody. “At this time, there is still no information to suggest that this is a terrorism related incident,” the force said.
Detectives remain “open-minded” as to potential motive, but there is no evidence to suggest the killing was politically motivated, the force added.
A 26-year-old man who was previously arrested on suspicion of murder had been released and was no longer part of the investigation, police said Saturday.

“Our murder enquiry is in its early stages but moving at a significant pace. We are deploying all of the necessary resources to find out exactly what has happened,” Assistant Chief Constable Matt Longman of Devon and Cornwall Police said.
Outgoing Prime Minister Keir Starmer said it was “shocking news,” while Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said she was “stunned” and “really struggled to find the words.”

Britain’s interior minister Shabana Mahmood said the circumstances of Widdecombe’s death were “extremely distressing” and urged the public “to avoid speculation and allow the police investigation to progress.”
But Nigel Farage, the leader of Reform UK, said he feared that “for anybody in public life, or especially the political space, things have become even more dangerous to them.”
“We don’t know what political motives are, whether they exist at all,” he said. “Was it a burglary gone wrong? We just don’t know.”

Farage received a £5 million ($6.7 million) gift in early 2024 from crypto billionaire donor Christopher Harborne, which he initially said in June 2026 was for his personal security, adding that he will need protection “until the day that I die.” He later said the gift was “unconditional.”
Britain’s parliamentary standards commissioner is investigating whether Farage broke the rules by not declaring the gift, which was made months before he became a member of Parliament.
For others, Widdecombe’s death sparked memories of the murders over the last decade of politicians Jo Cox and David Amess.
Cox’s husband, Brendan Cox, said Widdecombe’s death brought back “all of the pain and emotion” of losing his wife, a Labour MP who was murdered in 2016.

“We obviously don’t know and can’t speculate on the motivation, rationale and motive for the attack,” he wrote in Britain’s Daily Mirror newspaper. “But what we can say is that there is nothing that could ever justify an attack like this.”

Cox, 41, known for social justice campaigns and seen as a rising star in Britain’s Labour Party, was stabbed 15 times and received three gunshot wounds in a 2016 attack outside her constituency office in the town of Birstall in West Yorkshire, northern England.

Cox was a high-profile supporter of the campaign to stay in the European Union and to keep the debate from being hijacked by immigration. Thomas Mair, convicted in her murder, repeatedly shouted “Britain first” during the attack, the trial heard.

Five years later, Conservative lawmaker Amess was stabbed multiple times in 2021 by an attacker inspired by the Islamic State group. Ali Harbi Ali was given a whole-life sentence for the murder in 2022.

While the details of Widdecombe’s death remain unclear, it “certainly comes within the backdrop of MPs’ safety becoming more and more of a concern,” said Andrew Barclay, a politics lecturer at the University of Sheffield.

Beyond Cox and Amess, he added, other reported crimes against MPs “have more than doubled since the 2019 general election, and there have been several other notable cases of harassment since then, both physically and at scale over social media,” he told NBC News.
Tim Bale, a politics professor at Queen Mary University of London, said the U.K. was “generally, an unviolent society,” yet “almost we’ve had two MPs killed in the last 10 years.”
“We’re also a more politically polarized place than ever we used to be,” he said, and politicians have “also had to get used to people threatening them online and in person on the campaign trail.”
While it’s possible to exaggerate the risk, he added, “they are right to worry and right to ask for protection.”
The alarm was raised over Widdecombe on Wednesday when she failed to turn up for a remote television interview, Channel 5 presenter Dan Walker said on X.

“Ann was due to appear on 5 Daytime on Wednesday afternoon but stopped responding to messages and didn’t turn up for the show,” he said. “The team contacted her agent to ask them to check in on her. This information has been passed to police as it’s part of the investigation.”
The management company that represented Widdecombe after she left politics said her life and career were driven by strong Christian values and a commitment to public service.

“She loved the cut and thrust of political debate and, 16 years after leaving Parliament, was still actively campaigning for Reform UK and offering forthright views on the hot topics of the day,” Cloud9 Management said.

title: Metallic space balls found on Australian beach
summary: Mysterious metal spheres washed ashore in Australia, and officials say they’re literal space balls — but with no known connection to Mel Brooks’ “Spaceballs.”
story: Mysterious metal spheres washed ashore on a northern Australia beach, and officials say the unidentified floating objects are literal space balls — although there’s no known affiliation with the Mel Brooks comedy classic “Spaceballs.”
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.
Several of the metallic objects were discovered on Forrest Beach, a small quiet coastal town in Queensland, the Australian Space Agency announced Sunday on X.
The unknown objects were later identified as “space debris” by the ASA, most likely from a rocket that recently re-entered Earth’s atmosphere from orbit.
“The recovered objects appear to be pressure vessels from a space launch vehicle,” the agency said on X.
Queensland Fire and Resue said on X its crews closed off part of the beach to help partner agencies like the ASA inspect and recover the objects, which were determined to be safe.
Though unusual, space debris crashing into Earth is not uncommon.

It can be a result of a variety of space objects re-entering Earth, the ASA said on its official site, including satellites or space vehicles that do not completely burn up as they pass through the atmosphere.
